articles.title: Oscar Predictions: Best Casting — ‘Being Heumann’ and ‘La Bola Negra’ Found the Year’s Boldest Discoveries. Will the Academy Reward Them?
articles.summary: Variety Awards Circuit section is the home for all awards news and related content throughout the year, featuring the following: the official predictions for the upcoming Oscars, Emmys, Grammys and Tony Awards ceremonies, curated by Variety chief awards editor Clayton Davis.
body: Best Casting Predictions Commentary (Updated: Nov. 8, 2026): Casting is only in its second year as an Oscar category and if voters just default to whichever best picture front-runner had the splashiest ensemble, the whole point of the award might be flawed. One of the two films that stand out in this category sense, are “ Being Heumann,” Siân Heder’s Apple drama about Judy Heumann and the 1977 San Francisco sit-in that forced the government to enforce disability rights and “La Bola Negra,” Los Javis’ Netflix epic that threads three gay men across three eras of Spain.

For Heder’s film, casting directors Bernie Telsey and Adam Caldwell put more than 20 disabled actors on screen around breakout Ruth Madeley’s Judy, a lot of them with little or no acting experience, which is a bigger swing than any other star-studded ensemble.

Over in Spain, Eva Leira and Yolanda Serrano delivered Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi a cast where the pop singer Guitarricadelafuente makes his acting debut alongside newcomers Milo Quifes and Carlos González, then surrounded them with legends like Penélope Cruz and a Spanish-speaking Glenn Close. That’s discovery.

articles.title: Dave Chappelle’s Charlie Kirk Joke Prompts Response from Erika Kirk: Using the ‘Destruction of a Human Life’ as a ‘Punchline Is Beyond Disgusting’
articles.summary: After Dave Chappelle joked that he feels better ever since Charlie Kirk was murdered, Kirk’s widow, Erika, has responded to those using her late husband’s death as a punchline.
body: She continued: “A culture that laughs at assassination is one of profound moral decay. It threatens the very foundation of our country and the principles that hold our democracy together. You do not have to agree with someone’s politics to recognize the value of their life. This should not be so hard. Political violence must never be something this country tolerates, excuses, or celebrates.”

Chappelle has been receiving backlash across social media after footage from his Friday show at Madison Square Garden — which was advertised as a phone-free experience that would require devices be stored away in Yondr pouches – showed the comedian quipping about Kirk’s death.

“I’ve Had It” podcast hosts Jennifer Welch and Angie Sullivan also came under fire r ecently for laughing at a joke about Kirk during a Thursday episode of their show. The two released a joint statement on Saturday, writing that they “regret it” and “apologize.”
The conservative activist and Turning Point USA co-founder died on Sept. 10, 2025, after being shot during a college event in Utah. He was 31.

articles.title: ‘Avedon’ Review: Ron Howard’s Thrilling Documentary About Richard Avedon, the Great Photographer Who Turned Head-On Portraits Into an Art Form
articles.summary: "Avedon," Ron Howard’s documentary about the legendary photographer, is a fantastic movie. It’s the best documentary Ron Howard has made (my favorite before this: "The Beatles: Eight Days a Week — The Touring Years"), and it’s been edited in a way that’s so supple and artful that its technique…
body: Avedon was a paragon of high fashion and also the ultimate democratic humanist. The film explains that paradox and makes his images sing.

“Avedon” opens with an old clip of Richard Avedon, fixing that piercing bird-eye look of his into the camera as he explains, “I can say very little about photography. I follow no rules, no laws, and no advice.” He’s totally serious about that. We then get a montage, set to the funky martial beat of Spoon’s “I Turn My Camera On,” of Avedon portraits of the famous. John Lennon. Orson Welles. Michael Jordan. Elizabeth Taylor. Groucho Marx. Twiggy (in mid-air). Anjelica Huston. Marilyn Monroe lovingly embracing Arthur Miller. Truman Capote. J. Robert Oppenheimer.
points: "Avedon," Ron Howard’s documentary about the legendary photographer, is a fantastic movie.

articles.title: ‘Passing Strange’ Comes to Pasadena Playhouse: Creators Stew and Heidi Rodewald on the Rock Musical Reaching L.A. Almost Two Decades After Tony-Winning Broadway Run
articles.summary: “Passing Strange” will seem just a little less strange to theatergoers now than it might have when it opened on Broadway in 2007 and scored big wins at the Tonys, the Drama Desk Awards and the New York Drama Critics’ Circle Awards.
body: The two of you aren’t directly working on this Pasadena Playhouse direction, but more like watching appreciatively from afar how it’s going, right?

Stew: Oh, yeah. No, we wouldn’t dare. Zhailon Levingston was sweet enough at one point to invite us to peek in, but he’s a total visionary, so all we could do at this point would be drag it down. First he knows the play better than we do. Secondly, if you’ve ever seen his work, like the work he did in “Cats: The Jellicle Ball,” he’s honestly the last person I would give any advice to.
Rodewald: The way he talks about “Passing Strange” just makes us think: Whatever you’re going to do, you get it.

articles.title: Bluey’s Daley Pearson on how losing his brother inspired his new film: ‘He was the best thing ever to me’
articles.summary: Allen, the first live-action film from Pearson’s Ludo Studio, follows a man who met an alien as a kid – and becomes obsessed with bringing him back. Get our weekend culture and lifestyle email.
body: If, for whatever reason, you want to feel a bit sad, think too hard about what Elliott from ET would have been like as an adult. Or Coraline, or Matilda, or Chihiro, or those kids in Mary Poppins. The most amazing thing that ever happened in their lives – magic nanny, alien friend, psychic abilities, otherworldly adventures – was already over when they were kids. If that bad Harry Potter play taught us anything, they probably all grew into loser adults.

There are a lot of nods to ET in Allen (“pretty aggressive nods,” Pearson laughs) – obviously the premise but also the score and even the poster, which features Allen and Petey’s fingers reaching to one another, and a floating Cheezel in the middle.
When I tell him that ET is among my favourite films, the 42-year-old winces. “Oh, no,” he says, rubbing his chin. “OK, we’ll talk about that.”

articles.title: ‘I’ve seen people in my neighbourhood pulled out of their cars’: Ava DuVernay on the cruelty and brutality of Trump’s America
articles.summary: Ten years after her landmark political documentary 13th, the film-maker delivers a follow-up on the 14th amendment – and the Trump administration’s attempts to dismantle birthright citizenship.
body: When I ask Ava DuVernay how she kept her focus while making her new film – or how anyone does, when the onslaught of news, fake news and disputed facts seems designed to overwhelm – she starts to answer, then stops. Her eyes have filled with tears.

“I just got emotional, as you said that, because it was the film that saved me,” she says. “It’s been a very tough two years. I live in Los Angeles, and I’ve seen people in my neighbourhood pulled out of their cars. The lady who sells flowers next to my office was there one day, and the next day she wasn’t. People I know personally are literally hiding in their houses, like Anne Frank vibes … So when I would feel the rage and the fear, I put it into the film … And I just … I was doing something.”

articles.title: Patrick Dempsey's Thanksgiving Horror Movie Is Worth Revisiting This Holiday Season
articles.summary: If you want to watch a Thanksgiving movie that features amusingly gross deaths, Patrick Dempsey, and more, this Eli Roth horror flick should do the trick.
body: Eli Roth's 2023 slasher flick "Thanksgiving" follows various citizens of Plymouth, Massachusetts, as they find themselves being targeted by a killer dressed as the famed Pilgrim John Carver in the lead-up to the titular holiday. Realizing that these murders are related to a Black Friday trampling incident from the previous year (which led to three people dying), it falls to Plymouth's sheriff, Eric Newlon (Patrick Dempsey), to figure out who's been taking some Turkey Day-related revenge.

There aren't too many scary flicks centered around this particular holiday, but Roth's film has now joined the modest pantheon of Thanksgiving horror movies that includes Brad F. Grinter's schlock classic "Blood Freak," the utterly absurd "ThanksKilling," the pointed anticapitalist flick "Black Friday," and Oliver Blackburn's "Kristy." Indeed, Roth's "Thanksgiving" is the perfect horror movie to watch this November, or any November, really. Like most of his other R-rated offerings, its gore is gleefully over the top, and there's gallows humor present throughout.

articles.title: Patrick Stewart's '90s Fantasy Movie With Neve Campbell Is Streaming For Free
articles.summary: Neve Campbell starred opposite Patrick Stewart (as a ghost) in this '90s Oscar Wilde fantasy story adaptation, which you can currently stream for free.
body: An adaptation of Oscar Wilde's 1887 short story, Sydney Macartney's "The Canterville Ghost" aired on ABC on January 27, 1996, and, perhaps surprisingly, featured notable central roles for both the late legend Sir Patrick Stewart and Neve Campbell. Indeed, 1996 was a banner year for both actors, with Stewart appearing in the film "Star Trek: First Contact" and Campbell headlining two of the best teen movies of the 1990s over the same 12-month period (namely, "The Craft" and "Scream"). Stewart, of course, was already riding high professionally by that point. But for Campbell, this was the final vault before proper stardom following her breakout role on the hit series "Party of Five."
points: Neve Campbell starred opposite Patrick Stewart (as a ghost) in this '90s Oscar Wilde fantasy story adaptation, which you can currently stream for free.

articles.title: Denis Villeneuve Praises Creative Process Over AI Prompts and Stops Short of Naming New Bond at LACMA Art+Film Gala
articles.summary: The stars were out Saturday night at the milestone 15th annual fundraiser, presented once again by Gucci and featuring a night-ending performance by global superstar Rosé.
body: Museums are many things: cultural institutions that serve as sources of inspiration, exhibitions of creativity, reflections of humanity, bridges to the past and freeways to the future. For Denis Villeneuve, museums have “always been super food.”

“Every time I walk into one, I feel like a vampire sucking the energy from the walls. And, one way or another, it ends up in one of my films,” explained the blockbuster director while standing at a podium Saturday night on the grounds of one of his favorites, LACMA in Los Angeles.

Some boldfaced names not in the building still got shout-outs from the podium. Villeneuve recalled how, as a pre-teen growing up in Quebec, Canada, all of his pals were reading about hockey while he was obsessed with Steven Spielberg. “He became my hero,” he said. “Steven is the reason I’m standing here today, and I’m lucky enough now to be able to call him a friend. And then came James Cameron. These are titans.” He also name-checked fellow auteurs Alfonso Cuarón, Alejandro González Iñárritu and Chloé Zhao, “three fellow artists pushing the boundaries of cinematic expression in the most original ways.”

articles.title: Stephen Colbert Evacuated From Harvard Event Due to Fire Alarm After Being Accused of Crossing Picket Line
articles.summary: Dozens of Harvard Graduate Students Union members protested outside the event featuring the former late night host and famed cellist Yo-Yo Ma.
body: After Stephen Colbert was accused of crossing a picket line during a Harvard University event, the evening was cut short when someone pulled a fire alarm.
The former late night host joined famed cellist Yo-Yo Ma for a conversation on Thursday as part of the Office of the Arts’ “Learning from Performers” series.

When the pair decided to proceed with the event as scheduled in Sanders Theatre, dozens of Harvard workers protested outside. However, the planned 90-minute conversation abruptly ended about 40 minutes in when a fire alarm went off, Harvard Magazine reported. Colbert was then evacuated from the venue.

In a statement shared on social media, HGSU stated that it was not involved with the fire alarm. “The alarm was unrelated to HGSU’s picketing activity and we have no knowledge of its cause,” the union wrote. “Members at the picket were relieved to learn that no one inside was at risk.”

articles.title: This X-Men-Esque '80s Sci-Fi Series Launched Courteney Cox's Career
articles.summary: Before Courteney Cox joined the cast of Friends, she had a starring role in a one-season 1980s sci-fi show that shared some DNA with Marvel's X-Men.
body: The premise of James D. Parriott's 1985 superhero/comedy series "Misfits of Science," which featured a young Courteney Cox, will sound very familiar to fans of Marvel Comics' X-Men titles.

The series follows a human scientist named Dr. Billy Hayes (Dean Paul Martin), who has taken an interest in what he called "human anomalies," which are people who have been born with a variety of unpredictable superpowers. In the show's pilot episode, he assembles the main cast of powerful castoffs with the intention of studying them, but also helping them come to terms with their supernatural abilities.

The team was small but mighty. It included Dr. Hayes' lab partner, Dr. Lincoln (Kevin Peter Hall), who can shrink for a limited period. Additionally, Mark Thomas Miller plays "Johnny B" Bukowski, a rocker who can suck up electricity and who wears shades to cover his glowing eyes. He can throw lightning bolts.
points: Before Courteney Cox joined the cast of Friends, she had a starring role in a one-season 1980s sci-fi show that shared some DNA with Marvel's X-Men.
